# pattern: # Linux programs that do the job of a Windows program.
# TWO CLASSES, and the difference matters a great deal:
#   nativo   - IT IS THE SAME PROGRAM, with an official Linux build. There is
#              no swap and no adaptation: same product, same vendor, running
#              directly. Running it under Wine is always worse - slower, no
#              automatic updates, and it breaks when Wine changes. This is the
#              category that solves the most and that the fewest people know
#   parecido - A different program that does a similar job. It is NOT the
#              same, and the "what changes" column has to say how it differs.
#              Suggesting a swap without naming the difference would be
# Tandem NEVER swaps anything on its own, and never suggests replacing a
# program that is working. This surfaces in two situations: when the owner
# asks ("tandem alternativas"), and when the pre-flight recognises that a
# program will never work here - where staying quiet would leave the owner
# A new line requires no code changes.
# The class values (nativo/parecido) are on-disk format, compared by the
# shell: do not translate them. The name, install instructions and "what
# changes" columns are shown to the user, so they stay in Portuguese.
